situation:
You finished school this spring, you are looking for your first apartment, and you have no credit history of your own. You have an appointment with a tax preparer (judge) at MARBLE HILL TAX SERVICES, who works with new earners on what an offer will actually pay once taxes are settled.

You hold two offers. One is a salaried position two states away paying $46,000 a year, reported on an IRS Form W-2, with taxes withheld from every paycheck. The other is contract work in your current city at $30 an hour, reported on an IRS Form 1099, with no withholding and with hours that grow as your skills do.

You have $4,300 saved, set aside as an emergency fund a year ago, and prices on the same expenses have risen since, so it now covers less than it did. Taking the salaried offer two states away would spend about $3,200 of it on a moving truck, a first month's rent, and the double security deposit a landlord requires from a renter with no credit history.

Taking the contract work in your current city would leave the savings untouched and keep the lease your roommate planned to sign with you here, but your pay would arrive with no taxes withheld, so you would set aside your own quarterly tax payments. The preparer (judge) wants your recommendation and how each offer changes what you owe.

The preparer (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the preparer's questions, the preparer (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are a tax preparer at MARBLE HILL TAX SERVICES. Business background is the same as the situation above.

A new earner with two offers, one salaried and reported on an IRS Form W-2 and one contract and reported on an IRS Form 1099, is weighing a move two states away against staying put, with a single pool of savings covering either the relocation or an emergency. You want to hear how each offer changes what is owed at tax time and a clear recommendation.

After the participant has presented, you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: How would you tell your roommate what you decided?
What would you want your roommate to hear first?
